items.stem: Distinguish between 'empathy' and 'unconditional positive regard'.
items.answer: Empathy: the therapist's ability to understand the client's experiences as if they were the therapist's own. Unconditional positive regard: the therapist's warmth and acceptance of the client irrespective of what the client says or does.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'empathy' (the therapist's ability to understand the client's experiences as if they were the therapist's own.) and 1 mark for 'unconditional positive regard' (the therapist's warmth and acceptance of the client irrespective of what the client says or does.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about nature and process of psychotherapy is correct?
items.answer: Psychotherapy is a voluntary relationship between the one who seeks treatment and the one who treats.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: It is a voluntary relationship between the client and the therapist. It is a contractual relationship of limited duration. Empathy is understanding the client's experience from the client's point of view; sympathy is pity.
options: Sympathy and empathy mean the same in therapy.
The therapeutic relationship continues for life.
Psychotherapy is a voluntary relationship between the one who seeks treatment and the one who treats.
Psychotherapy is an involuntary relationship imposed on the client.

Consider the following statements about factors in healing, ethics and rehabilitation:
I. Therapists may disclose client details to anyone who asks.
II. The techniques adopted by the therapist and the therapeutic alliance both contribute to healing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Confidentiality is an ethical requirement. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: Read the case and answer. In a hostel for children, residents earn stars for tidying beds, and the stars can be exchanged for a film night. Name the therapy technique shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Token economy: tokens given for desired behaviour are exchanged for rewards, increasing that behaviour.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (token economy); 1 mark for the explanation (tokens given for desired behaviour are exchanged for rewards, increasing that behaviour).

items.stem: Accepting a client without conditions, whatever the client says, is called:
items.answer: unconditional positive regard
items.markingKey: (b) unconditional positive regard.
options: empathy
unconditional positive regard
insight
catharsis

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Psychoanalysis aims at insight.
Reason (R): Bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about nature and process of psychotherapy:
I. Psychotherapy aims at improving the client's self-awareness, decision making and acceptance of self.
II. The therapeutic relationship continues for life.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: It is a contractual relationship of limited duration.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about humanistic-existential, biomedical and alternative therapies:
I. Biomedical therapy includes medication such as antidepressants and antipsychotic drugs prescribed by a psychiatrist.
II. Logotherapy was developed by Carl Rogers.
III. Humanistic-existential therapies believe that people have a drive for personal growth and self-actualisation.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: It was developed by Viktor Frankl. III is correct.
options: I and III only
II and III only
I and II only
III only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on factors in healing, ethics and rehabilitation and answer the questions that follow.
"Release of emotions, or catharsis, contributes to healing. Confidentiality, informed consent and professional competence are ethical standards of psychotherapy. Rehabilitation includes occupational therapy, social skills training, cognitive retraining and vocational training."
(i) The client's motivation for change and the therapist's warmth are examples of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'social skills training' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Informed consent is required. (2)
items.answer: (i) non-specific factors in healing (ii) Rehabilitation in which patients develop interpersonal skills through role play and imitation. (iii) The client has a right to know the nature of the therapy and to agree to it voluntarily.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) non-specific factors in healing (ii) Rehabilitation in which patients develop interpersonal skills through role play and imitation. (iii) The client has a right to know the nature of the therapy and to agree to it voluntarily.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: Sigmund Freud – psychoanalysis
items.markingKey: (a) Sigmund Freud – psychoanalysis. Albert Ellis – rational emotive therapy; Joseph Wolpe – systematic desensitisation; Aaron Beck – cognitive therapy are the correct pairs for the others.
options: Sigmund Freud – psychoanalysis
Aaron Beck – rational emotive therapy
Albert Ellis – systematic desensitisation
Joseph Wolpe – cognitive therapy

items.stem: In the study of psychodynamic, behaviour and cognitive therapy, the term 'interpretation' refers to:
items.answer: The psychoanalyst's technique of pointing out unconscious material to the client through confrontation and clarification
items.markingKey: (c) 'interpretation' means the psychoanalyst's technique of pointing out unconscious material to the client through confrontation and clarification.
options: The client's unconscious attaching to the therapist of feelings once held towards significant figures in childhood
The contractual and limited-duration bond between the therapist and the client in which both work towards the client's well-being
The psychoanalyst's technique of pointing out unconscious material to the client through confrontation and clarification
A voluntary relationship between the client and the therapist whose purpose is to help the client solve psychological problems

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Empathy is important in therapy.
Reason (R): Behaviour therapy holds that psychological distress arises from faulty behaviour patterns or thought patterns.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both statements are true, but R deals with a different point and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about humanistic-existential, biomedical and alternative therapies is NOT correct?
items.answer: Electro-convulsive therapy is a routine first treatment for all disorders.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. It is used only when drugs are not effective, and only by a psychiatrist.
options: Electro-convulsive therapy is a routine first treatment for all disorders.
Yoga and meditation are among the alternative therapies used for stress and anxiety.
Kundalini yoga has been found useful in treating mental disorders.
Biomedical therapy includes medication such as antidepressants and antipsychotic drugs prescribed by a psychiatrist.

items.stem: "Rehabilitation is needed after active symptoms are reduced." Examine this statement with reference to factors in healing, ethics and rehabilitation.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Patients with severe disorders such as schizophrenia often suffer from negative symptoms and lack of skills.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (patients with severe disorders such as schizophrenia often suffer from negative symptoms and lack of skills.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: Alternative therapies are called alternative.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: They are alternatives to conventional drug or psychotherapy treatments.
items.markingKey: (a) They are alternatives to conventional drug or psychotherapy treatments.
options: They are alternatives to conventional drug or psychotherapy treatments.
Only a medically trained psychiatrist can prescribe drugs or administer ECT.
The client is seen as capable of growth and finds solutions in an accepting relationship.
Bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.

items.stem: What is meant by 'cognitive therapy' in the context of psychodynamic, behaviour and cognitive therapy?
items.answer: Aaron Beck's therapy that changes negative automatic thoughts and dysfunctional beliefs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cognitive therapy correctly explained as Aaron Beck's therapy that changes negative automatic thoughts and dysfunctional beliefs.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about factors in healing, ethics and rehabilitation is correct?
items.answer: Confidentiality, informed consent and professional competence are ethical standards of psychotherapy.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Alliance, catharsis and non-specific patient and therapist factors also contribute. Confidentiality is an ethical requirement. It is undertaken after the active symptoms are reduced.
options: Healing depends only on the technique used.
Rehabilitation begins before the active symptoms are reduced.
Confidentiality, informed consent and professional competence are ethical standards of psychotherapy.
Therapists may disclose client details to anyone who asks.

items.stem:
Statement: Empathy is important in therapy.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It lets the therapist understand the client's experience from the client's point of view.
items.markingKey: (d) It lets the therapist understand the client's experience from the client's point of view.
options: It is the belief about an event, not the event itself, that produces emotional distress.
The client shares personal and painful experiences that must be kept confidential.
Warmth and acceptance help the client open up without fear of judgement.
It lets the therapist understand the client's experience from the client's point of view.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on nature and process of psychotherapy and answer the questions that follow.
"Psychotherapy is practised only by persons trained under supervision. Psychotherapy is a voluntary relationship between the one who seeks treatment and the one who treats. The therapeutic relationship is built on trust and requires empathy and unconditional positive regard from the therapist."
(i) Which of these is NOT a characteristic of psychotherapy? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'empathy' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The client must be able to trust the therapist. (2)
items.answer: (i) The therapist may share personal relationships with the client outside therapy (ii) The therapist's ability to understand the client's experiences as if they were the therapist's own. (iii) The client shares personal and painful experiences that must be kept confidential.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The therapist may share personal relationships with the client outside therapy (ii) The therapist's ability to understand the client's experiences as if they were the therapist's own. (iii) The client shares personal and painful experiences that must be kept confidential.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about humanistic-existential, biomedical and alternative therapies is correct?
items.answer: Kundalini yoga has been found useful in treating mental disorders.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: It is used only when drugs are not effective, and only by a psychiatrist. It was developed by Viktor Frankl. The therapist is non-directive and reflects the client's feelings.
options: Electro-convulsive therapy is a routine first treatment for all disorders.
Logotherapy was developed by Carl Rogers.
Kundalini yoga has been found useful in treating mental disorders.
In client-centred therapy the therapist interprets the client's unconscious.

items.stem:
Statement: Psychoanalysis aims at insight.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.
items.markingKey: (b) Bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.
options: It is the belief about an event, not the event itself, that produces emotional distress.
Bringing repressed conflicts into consciousness helps the client resolve them.
The client is seen as capable of growth and finds solutions in an accepting relationship.
Relaxation is incompatible with anxiety and is paired with gradually increasing feared stimuli.
